issues.change: Metric YAML schema completely rewritten for MetricFlow
issues.action: Rewrite all metric definitions using the new type/type_params/filter format
issues.impact: All existing metric YAML definitions fail to parse in 1.6; the pre-1.6 UnparsedMetric fields (calculation_method, expression, sql, model, type: expression) and the rename_metric_attr compatibility shim were removed.

context.detection:
- Search every YAML file under models/ and any schema-file globs declared in dbt_project.yml
  (models/**/*.yml, models/**/*.yaml, plus any top-level metrics/ dir) for a `metrics:` block.
- Flag a metric as legacy (pre-1.6) if its entry uses ANY of these keys: `calculation_method`,
  `expression`, `sql`, `type: expression`, a top-level `type:` with the old enum
  (`count`/`sum`/...), `model:`, `timestamp:`, `time_grains:`, `dimensions:` directly on the
  metric, or `filters:` (the list-of-dict old form).
- The new MetricFlow schema instead uses `type:` with values simple|ratio|cumulative|derived
  plus a `type_params:` block. If a metric already has `type_params:`, it is migrated — skip it.
- Also grep packages.yml for `dbt_metrics` usage and models for `metrics.calculate(` /
  `metrics.develop(` macro calls — those depend on the old package and must be flagged too.
context.fixing:
- Rewrite each legacy metric into the new schema. Attribute mapping:
  - `calculation_method` -> `type`: sum/average/min/max/count/count_distinct/median become
    `type: simple` with `type_params.measure`; derived/expression become `type: derived` with
    `type_params.expr` and `type_params.metrics`.
  - `expression`/`sql` -> `type_params.measure` (the semantic measure name), or
    `type_params.expr` for a derived metric.
  - `model:` -> moves into a `semantic_models:` definition (see example below).
  - `filters:` -> `filter:` (a single `{{ Dimension(...) }}` string, or keep the WHERE fragment).
- Concrete before/after:
  BEFORE (1.5):
    metrics:
      - name: total_revenue
        calculation_method: sum
        expression: amount
        model: ref('orders')
        timestamp: order_date
        time_grains: [day, month]
        dimensions: [status]
  AFTER (1.6, MetricFlow):
    semantic_models:
      - name: orders
        model: ref('orders')
        defaults:
          agg_time_dimension: order_date
        entities:
          - name: order
            type: primary
        dimensions:
          - name: order_date
            type: time
            type_params: {time_granularity: day}
          - name: status
            type: categorical
        measures:
          - name: amount
            agg: sum
            agg_time_dimension: order_date
    metrics:
      - name: total_revenue
        type: simple
        type_params:
          measure: amount
- Derived example: `calculation_method: derived` + `expression: revenue - cost` becomes
  `type: derived` with `type_params: {expr: 'revenue - cost', metrics: [{name: revenue},
  {name: cost}]}`.
- Judgment-heavy: 1.6 requires a `semantic_models:` layer that did not exist in 1.5, so the
  measure/entity/dimension split cannot always be inferred mechanically.
- If you cannot confidently reconstruct the semantic model (e.g. the source model's grain or
  entities are ambiguous), do NOT guess — record the metric in the results report with
  the original YAML and the suggested new shape, and move on.
- After editing, run `dbt parse`. On a metric/semantic-model validation error, re-read it;
  reverting to legacy form is NOT an option (it won't parse in 1.6) — instead leave the
  semantic_model skeleton and flag it manual.
- Remove `dbt_metrics` / `metrics.calculate` usages and flag them as requiring the
  MetricFlow / Semantic Layer migration (out of scope for parse).

issues.change: Duplicate node names allowed across packages
issues.action: Disambiguate cross-package references with two-argument ref('package_name', 'model_name')
issues.impact: In 1.5 a flat manifest dict raised DuplicateResourceNameError; in 1.6 names are stored per-package, so a project and an installed package can legitimately share a model name. Single-argument ref() to a name that exists in more than one package becomes ambiguous (AmbiguousAliasError / wrong node).

context.detection:
- Only relevant if packages.yml / dependencies.yml declares packages.
- Build the set of model/seed/snapshot names defined in the local project (models/**/*.sql,
  seeds/**/*.csv, snapshots/**/*.sql).
- Where available, add the names exposed by installed packages under dbt_packages/*/models.
- Grep all .sql/.yml for single-argument `ref('name')` / `ref("name")` whose `name` collides
  with a name present in BOTH the local project and a package (or in two packages) — those are
  the ambiguous refs.
- If no packages are installed, mark skipped-not-present.
context.fixing:
- For each ambiguous single-arg ref, rewrite to the two-argument form
  `ref('<package_name>', '<model_name>')`.
- Choose the package the author intended; default to the local project's own model unless the
  surrounding SQL clearly consumes the package's version.
- Example: `ref('customers')` -> `ref('my_project', 'customers')` or
  `ref('dbt_utils', 'customers')`. Leave unambiguous refs untouched.
- After edits run `dbt parse`; a remaining AmbiguousAliasError names the offending ref and node.
- If you cannot determine which package is intended, record it in the results report
  rather than guessing — picking the wrong package silently changes lineage.

issues.change: collect_freshness macro return type changed
issues.action: Update any custom collect_freshness macro override to return the full result object (table + response) instead of just the table
issues.impact: In 1.6 core's default collect_freshness returns a dict-like {table, response} object; a custom override that returns only the agate table triggers a deprecation warning and will break source freshness in later versions.

context.detection:
- Grep macros/**/*.sql for a macro named `collect_freshness` (i.e. `{% macro collect_freshness(`
  or `{% macro <adapter>__collect_freshness(`).
- If none exists, the project uses core's implementation — mark skipped-not-present.
- If one exists, inspect its final `{{ return(...) }}` and flag it if it returns the query
  result table directly (e.g. `return(load_result('collect_freshness').table)` or
  `return(table)`) rather than the full result object.
context.fixing:
- Change the macro to capture the full result and return an object exposing both the table and
  the adapter response.
- Pattern: `{% set result = run_query(...) %}` then
  `{{ return({'table': result.table, 'response': result.response}) }}`.
- Mirror core's 1.6 signature: it returns `load_result('collect_freshness')`, which already has
  `.table` and `.response`.
- Simplest safe fix, if the override only existed to tweak the SQL: align the return statement
  with core 1.6's macro body.
- After editing run `dbt parse`.
- If the override is complex or the intended response object is unclear, record it in the
  results report with a pointer to core's 1.6 collect_freshness for reference.

issues.change: sslmode behavior changed; require/allow/prefer now map to verify-ca
issues.action: Review and update sslmode in profiles.yml (advisory)
issues.impact: In 1.6 the redshift_connector sslmode mapping changed: require/allow/prefer are treated as verify-ca, so connections that relied on the looser semantics may fail without a CA certificate.

context.detection:
- Connection-profile concern, not visible to dbt parse.
- Look for `sslmode:` under a redshift target in profiles.yml (usually ~/.dbt/profiles.yml, but
  also any in-repo profiles.yml or profiles template).
- Flag values `require`, `allow`, or `prefer`.
- If profiles.yml is not in the repo, this can only be advised, not edited.
context.fixing:
- ADVISORY — do not open a warehouse connection.
- If an in-repo profiles.yml exists, note (do not silently rewrite auth) that require/allow/prefer
  now behave as verify-ca.
- Advise the user to either provide a CA cert (`sslrootcert`) or set the intended sslmode
  explicitly (e.g. `disable` / `verify-ca` / `verify-full`) to match their security posture.
- Record in the results report with the target name and current sslmode value.
- Excluded from the dbt parse verify loop (connection behavior is not exercised by parse).

issues.change: Autocommit enabled by default (autocommit: True)
issues.action: Set autocommit: false in profiles.yml if you relied on 1.5's transactional behavior (advisory)
issues.impact: 1.6 restores pre-1.5 semantics: autocommit defaults to True, so DDL and standalone statements auto-commit. Projects that depended on 1.5's implicit transaction wrapping (e.g. multi-statement hooks meant to roll back together) change behavior.

context.detection:
- Connection-profile concern, not visible to dbt parse.
- Check the redshift target(s) in profiles.yml for an explicit `autocommit:` key.
- Grep macros/**/*.sql and models for pre-hook/post-hook/on-run-* blocks containing explicit
  BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK — these suggest the project relied on transactional grouping.
- If neither profiles.yml is available nor transactional hooks exist, mark skipped-not-present.
context.fixing:
- ADVISORY — do not connect to the warehouse.
- If the project shows reliance on transactional behavior, advise setting `autocommit: false` on
  the redshift target in profiles.yml and record it in the results report (with target
  name).
- Do not blanket-add autocommit:false — the 1.6 default is intentional for most projects.
- Excluded from the dbt parse verify loop.

issues.change: list_relations_without_caching rewritten with Redshift-native SQL
issues.action: Review the macro if you override it; edge-case results may differ
issues.impact: 1.6 replaces the Postgres-based relation listing with Redshift-native SQL. Projects that override redshift__list_relations_without_caching may diverge from the new base behavior on edge cases (late-binding views, external schemas).

context.detection:
- Grep macros/**/*.sql for an override named `list_relations_without_caching`,
  `redshift__list_relations_without_caching`, or `postgres__list_relations_without_caching`
  used by the redshift adapter.
- If no override exists, mark skipped-not-present — core's new implementation applies
  automatically and needs no code change.
context.fixing:
- If an override exists, compare it against dbt-redshift 1.6's
  redshift__list_relations_without_caching.
- If the override only reproduced the old Postgres query, recommend removing it to inherit the
  fixed native version.
- If it adds project-specific logic, port that logic onto the 1.6 base query.
- This is behavioral (warehouse-executed), so `dbt parse` passes regardless — record a
  manual-actions note asking the user to validate relation listing against a live Redshift.
- If unsure whether the override is still needed, flag it rather than deleting it.

issues.change: dbt clean errors when clean-targets include source paths or paths outside the project
issues.action: Remove source paths (e.g. models/, macros/) and any path outside the project directory from clean-targets in dbt_project.yml
issues.impact: dbt clean now raises an error instead of silently deleting the wrong directories when clean-targets references source paths or paths outside the project root

context.detection:
- Read dbt_project.yml's clean-targets list.
- Flag any entry that resolves (relative to the project root) to a configured source path
  (model-paths, seed-paths, macro-paths, etc.) or that resolves outside the project directory
  (e.g. ../shared, /absolute/path).
context.fixing:
- Remove the offending entries from clean-targets, keeping only build/output directories
  (e.g. target, dbt_packages, logs).
- Re-run dbt clean to confirm it no longer errors.

issues.change: New warning when --state and --target point to the same directory
issues.action: Fix --state/--target configuration so they reference distinct directories
issues.impact: WarnStateTargetEqual raised (informational) for previously silent misconfiguration; fatal under --warn-error

context.detection:
- This is a runtime CLI/job configuration issue, not a repo-source issue, so `dbt parse` cannot
  surface it. Detect by scanning invocation sites, not models.
- Grep the repo for `--state` and `--target` / `--target-path` in shell scripts, Makefiles, and
  `scripts/**/*.sh`.
- Also grep CI configs: `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `azure-pipelines.yml`, `tox.ini`.
- Check `dbt_project.yml` for a `target-path:` key (deprecated since 1.5 but may still be present).
- Check for `DBT_STATE` / `DBT_TARGET_PATH` env vars in CI.
- Flag any invocation where `--state` and `--target`/`--target-path` resolve to the same directory
  (commonly both set to `target/`).
- Note the value is frequently supplied outside the repo (dbt platform job definitions,
  orchestration tools), which parse cannot see.
context.fixing:
- Point `--state` at a directory separate from the run's `--target` — e.g. keep run output in
  `target/` and the comparison manifest in a distinct dir such as `state/` or `prod-artifacts/`.
- Concretely, in the offending script/CI step change the duplicated paths so a command like
  `dbt build --state ./state --target-path ./target` uses different dirs, and populate the state
  artifacts there.
- If the same-directory usage lives outside the repo (a dbt platform job command, an orchestration
  tool), it cannot be edited from the repo.
- For that out-of-repo case: record it in the results artifact (target/dbt_migration_results.json)
  as manual-required with the issue_id, the invocation location if known, and the suggested command
  change, then prompt the user.
- This change never requires a repo edit to pass `dbt parse`; it is advisory / out-of-repo only.

issues.change: Breaking contract changes on unversioned models now warn instead of error
issues.action: Add --warn-error (or version the models) to retain the previous hard-error behavior on breaking contract changes
issues.impact: Unversioned models with a breaking schema/contract change warn via warn_or_error() instead of erroring; CI that relied on the error to block may now pass silently

context.detection:
- Scan schema YAML (`models/**/*.yml`, `models/**/*.yaml`) for models declaring `contract:` with
  `enforced: true` that do NOT declare a `version:` / `versions:` block (i.e. unversioned).
- Those unversioned enforced-contract models are the ones whose breaking contract changes now only
  warn.
- Also detect reliance on the old error behavior: grep CI/scripts for `dbt build` / `dbt run`
  invocations that lack `--warn-error` or `--warn-error-options`.
- Those flags are what previously turned the contract breakage into a hard failure.
- This is a behavior/policy change; `dbt parse` stays clean either way, so detection is about intent,
  not parse errors.
context.fixing:
- Preferred: preserve strict behavior by adding `--warn-error` (or a scoped `--warn-error-options`
  targeting contract deprecations) to the relevant dbt invocation.
- If that invocation is defined outside the repo (dbt platform job command, orchestration tool), it
  cannot be edited here: record it in the results artifact (target/dbt_migration_results.json) as
  manual-required with the suggested flag, and prompt the user.
- Alternative in-repo fix: add a `version:` to the affected models — versioning makes breaking
  contract changes error again.
- But versioning reshapes ref() resolution and downstream references, so only do it when the user
  explicitly wants versioned models; note that trade-off in the results report rather than silently
  versioning.
- No edit is required for `dbt parse` to succeed.

issues.change: New warning for contracted models with bare numeric columns (no precision/scale)
issues.action: Add explicit precision and scale to numeric column data_types in enforced contracts (e.g. numeric(38,3))
issues.impact: Models with 'data_type: numeric' (or 'decimal') and no precision/scale in an enforced contract now emit a warning at parse time in 1.7

context.detection:
- In schema YAML (`models/**/*.yml`, `models/**/*.yaml`), find models with `contract:`
  `enforced: true` and columns whose `data_type` is a bare numeric type with no precision/scale.
- Match the data_type value (case-insensitive) against `^(numeric|decimal|number)$` (no parentheses).
- Types that already include `(p,s)` like `numeric(38,3)` are fine and must be left alone.
- Only columns inside enforced-contract models trigger the warning; bare numeric on non-contracted
  models is not affected.
context.fixing:
- For each flagged column, replace the bare type with an explicit precision/scale, e.g.
  `data_type: numeric` -> `data_type: numeric(38,3)`.
- Choose precision/scale from evidence in this order:
- (1) an existing cast in the model SQL (e.g. `cast(x as numeric(18,2))`) — match it;
- (2) the warehouse's documented default for unqualified numeric if the model is already built
  (Snowflake NUMBER default is (38,0); Redshift/Postgres NUMERIC default is (38,0));
- (3) if unknown, use a safe wide default `numeric(38,6)` and note the assumption in the results
  report.
- Preserve YAML quoting/style.
- After editing, run `dbt parse`; if it fails, the likely cause is a mismatched type name for the
  adapter (e.g. Snowflake prefers `number(38,3)`) — retry with the adapter-native spelling.
- If the correct precision genuinely cannot be determined, leave the column and record it in the
  results artifact (target/dbt_migration_results.json) as manual-required for the user to confirm.

issues.change: merge_exclude_columns bug fix: excluded columns now correctly inserted in WHEN NOT MATCHED
issues.action: Review incremental models using merge_exclude_columns; excluded columns are now populated on new-row inserts
issues.impact: Incremental merge with merge_exclude_columns now inserts ALL columns for new rows (previously excluded columns were omitted on INSERT); resulting table data changes

context.detection:
- Grep model config for `merge_exclude_columns` in `models/**/*.sql` config() blocks (e.g.
  `config(materialized='incremental', ... merge_exclude_columns=[...])`) and in schema YAML
  `config:` blocks.
- Only relevant when `materialized='incremental'` with the default `merge` strategy on the Redshift
  adapter.
- This is a behavior/warehouse change invisible to `dbt parse`; nothing makes parse fail.
context.fixing:
- No source edit is required to reach 1.8 or pass parse — the fix was in the adapter. The migration
  action is to flag semantics.
- For each model using merge_exclude_columns, new rows (WHEN NOT MATCHED) will now have the
  previously-excluded columns inserted with their source values instead of being left null/default.
- If the user intentionally relied on those columns being unset on insert, that assumption breaks.
- Record each occurrence in the results artifact (target/dbt_migration_results.json) as
  manual-required with the issue_id, the model path, the merge_exclude_columns list, and a note to
  verify the new insert behavior is acceptable.
- Real validation happens in the warehouse build-green test layer, not here.
- Do not modify the model unless the user confirms a semantic change is needed.

issues.change: --dry-run flag removed from dbt deps --add-package; use dbt deps --lock instead
issues.action: Replace `dbt deps --add-package ... --dry-run` invocations with `dbt deps --lock`
issues.impact: Commands using `dbt deps --add-package <pkg> --dry-run` will error in 1.8 (unknown option --dry-run)

context.detection:
- Grep the repo for `--dry-run` alongside `dbt deps`. Pattern: `dbt\s+deps[^\n]*--dry-run`
  and `--add-package[^\n]*--dry-run`.
- Most common locations: shell scripts, Makefiles, CI YAML (.github/workflows/*.yml,
  .gitlab-ci.yml, azure-pipelines.yml), Dockerfiles, tox.ini, pre-commit configs, docs/READMEs.
- PRIMARY RISK IS OUT OF REPO: the same command may live in dbt platform job definitions,
  orchestration tools (Airflow/Dagster/cron), or a developer's shell history — not scannable
  from the repo.
context.fixing:
- For every in-repo occurrence, rewrite `dbt deps --add-package <pkg>@<ver> --dry-run` to
  `dbt deps --lock` (resolves and writes package-lock.yml without installing).
- If the intent was only to preview resolution, `dbt deps --lock` is the direct replacement.
- `dbt deps` does not affect `dbt parse`, so no parse retry loop applies here.
- ALWAYS add a manual-actions entry: issue_id, the fact that `--dry-run` on
  `dbt deps --add-package` now errors, and the instruction to audit all scheduled/CI job
  commands for `dbt deps ... --dry-run` and switch them to `dbt deps --lock`.

issues.change: Primary key constraint on multiple columns or at both column and model level now throws ParsingError
issues.action: Fix constraint definitions to specify the primary key in exactly one place
issues.impact: Models with duplicate/ambiguous primary_key constraint definitions fail to parse in 1.8 (ParsingError)

context.detection:
- Only relevant to models with `contract: {enforced: true}` (or constraints blocks).
- Scan model YAML (models/**/*.yml, *.yaml) and in-file `{{ config(...) }}` blocks for a
  primary key declared more than once.
- Failure shape 1: a model-level `constraints:` entry of `type: primary_key` listing multiple
  columns AND a column also carrying `constraints: [{type: primary_key}]`.
- Failure shape 2: more than one column each carrying a `type: primary_key` column-level
  constraint.
- Cues: search YAML for `type: primary_key` and count occurrences per model; also check for a
  model-level `constraints:` list with `- type: primary_key` combined with any column-level one.
- Composite PKs must be expressed once, at the model level, with `columns: [a, b]`.
context.fixing:
- Consolidate to a single primary key declaration per model.
- If a composite key is intended, remove the per-column `type: primary_key` constraints and
  declare one model-level constraint:
    constraints:
      - type: primary_key
        columns: [col_a, col_b]
- If a single-column PK is intended, keep exactly one declaration (column-level OR a model-level
  single-column entry) and delete the duplicate.
- Preserve any accompanying constraints (not_null, foreign_key) unchanged.
- After editing, run `dbt parse`; if it still raises a primary-key ParsingError, re-read the
  error's node name and ensure only one primary_key exists across column- and model-level.
- If the intended key is ambiguous (e.g. two different single-column PKs on one model), do not
  guess — record a manual-actions entry with the model name and the competing declarations.

issues.change: Spaces in resource names produce deprecation warning (SpacesInResourceNameDeprecation)
issues.action: Rename resources to remove spaces and rewrite all ref()/source() calls that reference them
issues.impact: SpacesInResourceNameDeprecation is raised at parse time in 1.8 for any model/seed/snapshot/source/test/exposure/metric whose name contains a space; treated as an error under --warn-error and slated for removal

context.detection:
- Two sources of resource names to scan.
- FILE NAMES: any `models/**/*.sql`, `models/**/*.py`, `seeds/**/*.csv`, `snapshots/**/*.sql`,
  `analyses/**/*.sql`, or `macros/**/*.sql` whose filename stem contains a space — the
  model/seed/snapshot name defaults to the filename. Glob for basenames matching `* *`.
- EXPLICIT NAMES in YAML: in models/**/*.yml and *.yaml, any `name:` value under models:,
  seeds:, snapshots:, sources: (both the source `name:` and each table `name:`), exposures:,
  metrics:, and named singular/data tests. Regex: `^\s*name:\s+.*\S \S`.
- `alias:` need NOT change (aliases may contain spaces if quoted) — the deprecation targets the
  resource NAME.
- Build a map of {old_name -> new_name} for every offending resource before editing anything.
context.fixing:
- For each offending resource, choose a new name by replacing spaces with underscores
  (e.g. `customer orders` -> `customer_orders`), keeping it unique. Then apply ALL of:
- (a) Rename the file if the name came from the filename:
    git mv 'models/customer orders.sql' models/customer_orders.sql
- (b) Update the `name:` (and matching properties block) in YAML.
- (c) Rewrite EVERY reference across the repo — `ref('customer orders')` ->
  `ref('customer_orders')`, and for source tables `source('src', 'my table')` ->
  `source('src', 'my_table')` — covering single- and double-quote forms in .sql/.py models and
  in `--select`/YAML selectors inside the repo.
- Example before: `select * from {{ ref('customer orders') }}`
- Example after:  `select * from {{ ref('customer_orders') }}`
- You MUST rewrite refs in the same pass as the rename, or `dbt parse` fails with an unresolved
  ref.
- After edits run `dbt parse`; if it fails with 'depends on a node named X which was not found',
  a ref still points at the old name — grep the repo for the old name and fix the stragglers.
- OUT-OF-REPO RISK: names are also referenced by dbt platform job `--select` clauses,
  `selectors.yml` consumed by CI, BI tools, and dbt Mesh cross-project refs
  (`ref('project', 'name')`). These cannot be rewritten from this repo.
- For every renamed resource, add a manual-actions entry listing old_name -> new_name and
  telling the user to update job selectors, downstream mesh refs, and BI tool references.
- If a name cannot be safely changed because too many external consumers depend on it, leave it
  and record a manual-required entry instead.

issues.change: Redshift catalog query macros restructured and split into multiple files
issues.action: Update custom overrides of redshift__get_base_catalog / catalog macros to match the new 1.8 structure
issues.impact: Custom overrides of redshift__get_catalog / redshift__get_base_catalog (and related catalog SQL) may break or silently diverge because the macro was split across a catalog/ directory in dbt-redshift 1.8

context.detection:
- Only relevant if the project (or an installed package) overrides Redshift catalog macros.
- Grep macros/**/*.sql and packages' macros for definitions named `redshift__get_catalog`,
  `redshift__get_base_catalog`, `redshift__get_catalog_relations`, or any
  `{% macro redshift__...catalog...%}`.
- If no such override exists, the change is not present (docs generate keeps working on the
  built-in macros).
- If an override exists, it likely mirrors the old single-file catalog.sql shape and will not
  align with the 1.8 split.
context.fixing:
- If an override is found, compare it against the dbt-redshift 1.8 catalog macros (now under an
  adapter catalog/ directory, split into base-catalog and relations pieces).
- Re-implement the override on the new macro seams: typically split a monolithic
  `redshift__get_catalog` override into `redshift__get_base_catalog` plus the relation-scoped
  variant, matching the new signatures.
- Invisible to `dbt parse` (catalog macros only compile when catalog generation runs), so parse
  cannot validate correctness.
- After adjusting, note that `dbt docs generate` against a warehouse is the real check (harness
  build-green layer, not in-skill).
- If the override's intent is unclear or reproducing the split is risky, record a manual-actions
  entry pointing at the overriding macro and the dbt-redshift 1.8 catalog macro source.

issues.change: require_explicit_package_overrides_for_builtin_materializations defaults to True
issues.action: Set the flag to false in dbt_project.yml flags: to keep old behavior, or update packages that override built-in materializations
issues.impact: Installed packages can no longer silently override built-in materializations (table/view/incremental); built-in takes precedence

context.detection:
- Check dbt_project.yml `flags:` for
  require_explicit_package_overrides_for_builtin_materializations.
- Check installed packages (dbt_packages/, packages.yml) for materialization overrides of
  table/view/incremental.
context.fixing:
- Handled by `dbt-autofix deprecations` (sets the flag explicitly). Review the diff.
- Manual fallback: add `require_explicit_package_overrides_for_builtin_materializations: false`
  under `flags:` to preserve old behavior, or update the offending package.
- Parse-detectable via the deprecation/warning; confirm clean on 1.8.

issues.change: tests config deprecated in favor of data_tests
issues.action: Rename `tests:` to `data_tests:` in dbt_project.yml and schema YAML files
issues.impact: `tests:` key emits a deprecation warning in 1.8; still works but slated for removal

context.detection:
- Grep dbt_project.yml for a top-level `tests:` block.
- Grep models/**/*.yml for `tests:` keys (both model-level and column-level).
context.fixing:
- Handled by `dbt-autofix deprecations` (renames `tests:` -> `data_tests:`).
- Review the diff and confirm every occurrence was renamed (leave the test list contents
  unchanged).
